questions.question: A can do a work in 72 days and B in 90 days. If they work on it together for 10 days, then what fraction of work is left?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(72, 90) = 360 units.

Efficiency: A = 360/72 = 5, B = 360/90 = 4; Total efficiency = 9 units/day.

Work done in 10 days = 9 × 10 = 90 units.

Remaining work = 360 − 90 = 270 units.

Fraction of work left = 270 ÷ 360 = 3/4.

**∴ The correct answer is 3/4.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: A completes work in 72 days and B in 90 days.

Formula: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**

 90
 4
 
 

⇒ Combined Efficiency of A and B = 5 + 4 = 9 units/day.

⇒ Work completed by A and B together in 10 days = 10 × 9 = 90 units.

⇒ Remaining work = Total Work − Work Completed

⇒ Remaining work = 360 − 90 = 270 units.

⇒ Fraction of work left = Remaining Work ÷ Total Work

⇒ Fraction = 270 ÷ 360 = 3/4.

**∴ The correct answer is 3/4.**

**__Additional Information__**

One Day's Work Principle

If a person completes a task in 'n' days, then the work done in 1 day is 1/n fraction of the total work.

Work and Wages Relationship

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done by each person, which is proportional to their efficiency if they work for the same duration.

Negative Work in Pipes and Cisterns

In similar problems involving inlet and outlet pipes, the outlet pipe's efficiency is taken as negative work since it empties the tank.</p

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 18 days, B and C in 24 days, A and C in 36 days. Working together they can do the work in
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

LCM of 18, 24, and 36 = 72 units (Total Work)

Efficiency (A+B) = 72 ÷ 18 = 4 units/day

Efficiency (B+C) = 72 ÷ 24 = 3 units/day

Efficiency (A+C) = 72 ÷ 36 = 2 units/day

Sum of efficiencies: 2(A+B+C) = 4 + 3 + 2 = 9 ⇒ (A+B+C) = 4.5 units/day

Time taken by (A+B+C) together = 72 ÷ 4.5 = 16 days

**∴ The correct answer is 16 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (A + B) = 18 days

Time taken by (B + C) = 24 days

Time taken by (A + C) = 36 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let efficiencies of A, B, and C be a, b, and c respectively.

⇒ (a + b) + (b + c) + (a + c) = 4 + 3 + 2

⇒ 2(a + b + c) = 9

⇒ a + b + c = 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5

⇒ Combined efficiency of A, B, and C together = 4.5 units/day

⇒ Time taken by (A + B + C) = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time = 72 ÷ 4.5

⇒ Time = 16 days

**∴ The correct answer is 16 days.**

Individual Time Calculation

To find A's individual efficiency, subtract (B+C) efficiency from (A+B+C) efficiency: Efficiency of A = 4.5 − 3 = 1.5. Time for A = 72 ÷ 1.5 = 48 days.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done or the ratio of efficiencies when the time period of work is the same for all.

Pipes and Cisterns

Similar to Time and Work, but outlet pipes have negative efficiency. Total capacity of the tank acts as the Total Work.</p

questions.question: Working 7 hours in a day, 4 men can do a piece of work in 8 days. Working 8 hours in a day, the required number of men to perform the same work in 4 days will be
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the Chain Rule: M₁ × D₁ × H₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂

Substitute the values: 4 × 8 × 7 = M₂ × 4 × 8

Cancel out common factors (4 × 8) from both sides: M₂ = 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7 men.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial condition: M₁ = 4 men, D₁ = 8 days, H₁ = 7 hours/day

Final condition: D₂ = 4 days, H₂ = 8 hours/day, M₂ = ?

**Formula used:**

Product of workers, time, and days remains constant for the same work: M₁ × D₁ × H₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9daa527a2d9ce782793a0ec6f5efc4d0439b433af887839f9dc26667a4afc226.png] 

⇒ 4 × 8 × 7 = M₂ × 4 × 8

⇒ 224 = M₂ × 32

⇒ M₂ = 224 ÷ 32

⇒ M₂ = 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7 men.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

General Chain Rule Formula

The complete formula for work comparison is (M₁ × D₁ × H₁ × E₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂ × E₂) ÷ W₂, where E is efficiency and W is work.

Inverse Proportion in Work

The number of men is inversely proportional to the number of days or hours required to complete a fixed amount of work.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each person, which is the product of their efficiency and time spent.</p

questions.question: A canal of a village can be cleaned by 24 villagers in 12 days. The number of days in which 36 villagers can clean the canal is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the constant work formula: M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂

24 × 12 = 36 × Days

Days = (24 × 12) ÷ 36 = 288 ÷ 36

Days = 8 days

**∴ The correct answer is 8 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Villagers₁ (M₁) = 24, Days₁ (D₁) = 12, Villagers₂ (M₂) = 36

Formula: Total Work = Men × Days

⇒ Total Work = 24 × 12 = 288 units

⇒ Required Days = Total Work ÷ M₂

⇒ Required Days = 288 ÷ 36

⇒ Required Days = 8 days

**∴ The correct answer is 8 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

The Chain Rule

Work problems involving men, days, and hours are solved using (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) / W₂.

Inverse Variation in Work

When the amount of work is constant, the number of people is inversely proportional to the time taken (M ∝ 1/D).</p

questions.question: A can do 1 / 5 of a job in 10 days, B can do 1 / 3 rd of the job in 25 days. In how many days can they do half of the job working together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A takes 10 × 5 = 50 days and B takes 25 × 3 = 75 days for full job.

Total work (LCM of 50, 75) = 150 units.

Combined efficiency of A and B = 3 + 2 = 5 units/day.

Time for full job = 150 ÷ 5 = 30 days.

Time for half job = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A does 1/5 of the job in 10 days.

B does 1/3 of the job in 25 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time; Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Days

⇒ Time taken by A for full job = 10 × 5 = 50 days.

⇒ Time taken by B for full job = 25 × 3 = 75 days.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**

⇒ Total Efficiency (A + B) = 3 + 2 = 5 units/day.

⇒ Half of the Total Work = 150 ÷ 2 = 75 units.

⇒ Time taken to complete half job = 75 ÷ 5 = 15 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Work Formula

For two people A and B taking 'a' and 'b' days respectively, combined time taken is (a × b) ÷ (a + b).

Work and Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is the reciprocal of the time taken to complete a task. Efficiency ∝ 1 / Time.

Partial Work Rule

If a person completes 1/n part of work in D days, the total time taken for the full work is n × D days.</p

questions.question: A and B worked together and received a total of Rs. 18,000 for 15 days. A's efficiency in the work was 5 times that of B's. The daily wage of A (in Rs.) was:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total daily wage of A and B = 18,000 ÷ 15 = ₹1,200.

Efficiency Ratio (A : B) = 5 : 1.

Wages are distributed in the ratio of efficiency: Total parts = 5 + 1 = 6.

Value of 6 parts = 1,200 → 1 part = 200.

Daily wage of A = 5 parts = 5 × 200 = ₹1,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount received = ₹18,000

Number of days worked = 15 days

Efficiency of A = 5 × Efficiency of B

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ea5bf4cf50a9085505c3ce580480595a184d5310c52f8f2ef046197621dd3e6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Daily wage of (A + B) = Total Wage ÷ Number of days

⇒ Daily wage of (A + B) = 18,000 ÷ 15 = ₹1,200

⇒ Let B's daily efficiency be 1x, then A's daily efficiency = 5x

⇒ Total efficiency = 5x + 1x = 6x

⇒ Since daily wage is proportional to efficiency: 6x = 1,200

⇒ x = 1,200 ÷ 6 = 200

⇒ Daily wage of A = 5x = 5 × 200 = ₹1,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Wage Distribution Rule

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done, which is the product of Efficiency × Time. If time is the same for all workers, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Efficiency and Work Relation

Work = Efficiency × Time. Efficiency is the amount of work done in a single unit of time (per day, per hour, etc.).

Ratio and Proportion in Wages

If the ratio of efficiencies of two workers is a : b, their shares of the total wage will be [a/(a+b)] × Total Wage and [b/(a+b)] × Total Wage respectively.

questions.question: A and B can do a work together in 18 days. A is three times as efficient as B. In how many days can B alone complete the work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency Ratio (A : B) = 3 : 1

Combined Efficiency (A + B) = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day

Total Work = Combined Efficiency × Combined Time = 4 × 18 = 72 units

Days taken by B alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B = 72 ÷ 1 = 72 days

**∴ The correct answer is 72 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Time taken by A and B together = 18 days. A is three times as efficient as B.

Formula Used: Total Work = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Let the efficiency of B be 1 unit/day.

⇒ Then, efficiency of A = 3 × 1 = 3 units/day.

⇒ Total efficiency of A and B = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day.

⇒ Total work = Combined efficiency × Number of days taken together = 4 × 18 = 72 units.

⇒ Time taken by B alone = Total work ÷ B’s efficiency = 72 ÷ 1 = 72 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 72 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Efficiency-Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If Efficiency ratio is a : b, then Time ratio is b : a.

Combined Work Formula

If A does a work in ’x’ days and B does it in ’y’ days, then together they take (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.

Man-Days Concept

The amount of work is proportional to the product of efficiency and duration, expressed as M₁D₁ = M₂D₂.</p

questions.question: **A **and **B **together can do a piece of work in 12 days. **A** alone can do it in 18 days. In how many days can **B **alone can do the work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct formula for finding the time of the second person when combined time and one person's time are given:

Days taken by B = (X × Y) ÷ (Y − X)

Where X = combined days of A and B = 12, and Y = days of A alone = 18.

Days taken by B = (18 × 12) ÷ (18 − 12) = (18 × 12) ÷ 6 = 3 × 12 = 36 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (A + B) = 12 days

Time taken by A alone = 18 days

 
 

 **Person**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work = LCM of 12 and 18 = 36 units.

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B) = Total Work ÷ Days = 36 ÷ 12 = 3 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of A = Total Work ÷ Days = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of B = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of A = 3 − 2 = 1 unit/day.

⇒ Time taken by B alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time taken by B alone = 36 ÷ 1 = 36 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. If the ratio of efficiency is x:y, the ratio of time taken is y:x.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done or in the ratio of efficiencies when the time period of work for all workers is the same.

Pipes and Cisterns

The same LCM logic applies where filling pipes have positive efficiency and leakage or outlet pipes have negative efficiency.</p

questions.question: Three men and 4 women can do a piece of work in 7 days, whereas 2 men and 1 woman can do it in 14 days. Seven women will complete the same work in:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Equate total work: (3M + 4W) × 7 = (2M + 1W) × 14

⇒ 3M + 4W = 2(2M + 1W) ⇒ 3M + 4W = 4M + 2W ⇒ 1M = 2W

Total work in terms of women = (3 × 2W + 4W) × 7 = 70W

Number of days for 7 women = 70W ÷ 7W = 10 days

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (3M + 4W) complete work in 7 days; (2M + 1W) complete work in 14 days.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Efficiency × Time; Efficiency × Time = Constant

 
 

 **Group**
 **Days**
 **Total Work (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**

⇒ Efficiency of 3M + 4W = 2 −−− (i)

⇒ Efficiency of 2M + 1W = 1 −−− (ii)

⇒ From (i) and (ii): 3M + 4W = 2(2M + 1W)

⇒ 3M + 4W = 4M + 2W ⇒ 1M = 2W

⇒ Substitute M = 2W in (ii): 2(2W) + 1W = 1 ⇒ 5W = 1 ⇒ W = 1/5 unit/day

⇒ Efficiency of 7 women = 7 × W = 7 × (1/5) = 7/5 units/day

⇒ Time taken by 7 women = Total Work ÷ Efficiency = 14 ÷ (7/5)

⇒ Time = 14 × (5/7) = 10 days

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

M-D-H Relation

For group work, use (M₁×D₁×H₁)/W₁ = (M₂×D₂×H₂)/W₂ to compare different sets of workers and work done.

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the same amount of work. If Time ratio is x:y, Efficiency ratio is y:x.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done by individuals, which is (Efficiency × Time).</p

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 9 days. B and C can complete the same work in 12 days and 18 days respectively. If A, B, C work together, then in how many days will they complete the work?
questions.solution:
Given

A can finish a work in 9 days

B can finish a work in 12 days

C can finish a work in 18 days

Concept

Men × efficiency = work

Calculation

Work done by A in one day(A) = (1/9) ---- (1)

work done by B in one day(B) = 1/12 ---- (2)

work done by C in one day(C) = 1/18 ---- (3)

Adding (1), (2) and (3)

⇒ A + B + C = (1/9) + (1/12) + (1/18)

⇒ A + B + C = (4 + 3 + 2)/36

⇒ (A + B + C) = 9/36

⇒ (A + B + C) = 1/4

⇒ A + B + C = 1/4

1/4th work is done by A, B and C in one day. so, Total work done by A, B and C in 4 days.

∴ A, B and C finish the work together in 4 days.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** 

LCM of (9,12 and 18) = Total work done = 36

Efficiency of A = 36/9 = 4

Efficiency of B = 36/12 = 3

Efficiency of A = 36/18 = 2

Together, work will be done in = 36/(4 + 3 + 2) = 4 days.
